ingredients.name: pecorino romano
ingredients.original: 160 g pecorino romano, very finely grated

ingredients.name: coarse salt
ingredients.original: 1 tsp coarse salt, for the pasta water

steps.text: Toast the crushed pepper in a dry pan until fragrant. Add a ladle of pasta water and take off the heat.
Cook the pasta in a small amount of lightly salted water so it gets very starchy. Save plenty of water.
Mash the pecorino with a few spoons of warm (not boiling) pasta water to a smooth paste.
steps.critical: Water must be warm, not boiling, or the cheese clumps into strings.

steps.text: Toss the pasta in the pepper pan, then off the heat add the cheese paste and toss hard, adding water until creamy.

notes.techniques: The whole dish is an emulsion of cheese, starch and water. Use less water than usual so it gets starchy, and slightly salted since pecorino is salty.
notes.chemistry: Pecorino proteins clump above about 65 °C. Starch from the pasta water coats the fat and protein so they stay dispersed in a creamy sauce.
notes.spiceProfile: Toasted black pepper is the only spice, sharp against salty sheep's cheese.
notes.variations: The Roman purist version: only pecorino, pepper and pasta water, with no butter or oil.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.original: 1 tsp salt, for the pasta water

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti in lightly salted water until 1 minute short of al dente. Save 3 dl of water.
Melt the butter, toast the pepper in it, then add 1 dl of pasta water.
Finish cooking the pasta in the pan for a minute. Off the heat, add the cheeses in handfuls, tossing and adding water until creamy.
steps.critical: Take the pan off the heat before adding the cheese.

notes.techniques: Butter gives the sauce extra fat to emulsify around, making it much more forgiving.
notes.chemistry: Butter adds emulsifiers and fat that keep cheese proteins from clumping when the pan is a little too hot.
notes.spiceProfile: Mellower than the classic: parmesan softens the sharp pecorino.
notes.variations: A forgiving version with butter and part parmesan. Less sharp but much less likely to clump.
